meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 13 (Multi-Select): Extensions (MCP Apps, Tasks, Auth Extensions)
meta.format: multi_select: questions use the 'answers' array (multiple correct options). Some include an 'All of the above' option that is only correct when every other option is.

questions.question: Which elements make up the MCP Apps security model? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Mandatory sandboxed iframes for all UI content
A host-constructed CSP from server-declared domains, defaulting to deny-all network when nothing is declared
Auditable JSON-RPC-over-postMessage communication between UI and host
UI-triggered tool calls go through the host's ordinary audit and consent path
UI resources fetch data directly from the internet, bypassing the host

questions.explanation: The whole point of the model is that nothing bypasses the host: sandboxed iframes, declared-domain CSP (hosts may tighten, never loosen), auditable messaging, and consent-gated tool calls.

questions.question: Which task statuses are TERMINAL in the Tasks extension? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: completed
failed
cancelled
working
input_required

questions.explanation: completed, failed, and cancelled are terminal — once reached, state never changes. working and input_required are in-progress states.

questions.question: Which obligations does the Tasks extension place on a consuming CLIENT? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Declare io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks in its per-request capabilities
Handle polymorphic results: a supported request may return either the normal result or a CreateTaskResult
Poll tasks/get respecting pollIntervalMs until a terminal status
Persist task IDs durably so polling survives a crash or restart
Send tasks/result to block until completion

questions.explanation: tasks/result was the old blocking method removed in the redesign — polling via tasks/get replaced it. The other four are the documented client steps (plus answering input_required via tasks/update).

questions.question: Which statements about the extensions framework are true? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Extensions are always opt-in, requiring explicit support from both client and server
Identifiers follow {vendor-prefix}/{extension-name}; official ones use io.modelcontextprotocol
Official extensions live in MCP GitHub org repos prefixed ext-
An extension support matrix documents which clients implement which official extensions
Any server may silently enable an extension for clients that never declared it

questions.explanation: Negotiation is mandatory in both directions — e.g., a server must never return a task to a client that didn't declare the tasks extension.

questions.question: Which method names exist in the redesigned Tasks extension? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: tasks/get — poll current state and, at terminal status, the result or error
tasks/update — supply inputResponses for an input_required task
tasks/cancel — cooperative cancellation intent
tasks/list — enumerate all tasks on the server
All of the above

questions.explanation: tasks/list existed in the experimental core feature and was removed in the extension redesign (SEP-2663), along with the blocking tasks/result.

questions.question: Which statements about MCP Apps resources are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: UI resources use the ui:// URI scheme
The MIME type is text/html;profile=mcp-app
A tool links to its UI via _meta.ui.resourceUri
The View communicates with the host via JSON-RPC over postMessage
All of the above

questions.explanation: The full linkage chain is accurate end to end — a true all-of-the-above.

questions.question: Which properties does the Tasks extension require of task IDs and task creation? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Task IDs are generated with sufficient entropy to prevent enumeration
The task must be durably created (findable via tasks/get) before the CreateTaskResult is sent
The CreateTaskResult carries taskId, initial status, ttlMs, and pollIntervalMs
Servers may return a task to any client, since tasks are server-directed
All of the above

questions.explanation: Server-directed creation is still capability-gated: a task must never go to a client that didn't declare io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks in its per-request capabilities.

questions.question: Which auth extension matches which deployment need? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Nightly unattended data-sync agent → OAuth Client Credentials (io.modelcontextprotocol/oauth-client-credentials)
Company-wide zero-touch server provisioning via the IdP → Enterprise-Managed Authorization
EMA lets the IdP scope access by user group (e.g., engineering read-only vs marketing read/write)
Both extensions activate by default whenever a server advertises them
All of the above

questions.explanation: Extensions are never active by default — the client must declare support. That false D takes E down with it.
